proof.claim:
A node that missed several generations must converge FORWARD, and must never
be treated as evidence that its old generation should be restored.

THE FAULT. Stop a node. While it is down, advance the cluster through several
desired-state changes. Restart it.

    node-5 down, holding a complete and internally consistent view of
    generation N
          ↓
    cluster advances: N → N+1 → N+2 → N+3
          ↓
    node-5 returns, still coherent, still wrong

WHY THIS IS NOT ORDINARY REJOIN. etcd-member-resync already covers a member
catching up on writes it missed, and compute-node-rejoin covers a node coming
back. Both return a node to a cluster whose desired state it merely lags.
This returns a node holding an ALTERNATE HISTORY: locally complete, internally
consistent, and contradicted by the cluster.

The law under test is the one that makes local state safe to keep at all:

    local persisted state is evidence of what happened,
    never authority over what should happen.

A node that returns with generation N must be read as an observer of the
current generation, not as a witness that N should be reconstructed. The
failure mode this hunts is a returning node whose stale local records win a
merge, or whose reappearance makes the controller re-derive an older desired
state from installed evidence.

WHAT MUST HOLD. The returning node ends on the cluster's current generation,
the desired state written while it was away is unchanged, no drift storm
follows, and the cluster is healthy with every node accounted for.
